description: Context-window compaction and transcript offload fidelity, measured black-box. Each task pins a small agent-level context window (2000 tokens, summarization trigger at 75%), then builds one long measured thread — the seeding turns and the recall question ride in the same session, because the runner scopes setup chat_turns to a separate logical session from the measured one, so only measured turns reach the context under test; the harness compacts mid-thread and the final turn asks for an early-seeded fact. Soundness under pooled-answer verification: the file-write probes (transcript_file_write) are immune to seed-turn acknowledgements echoing seeded values, so every task pairs its answer probe with a file leg. All seeded tokens are short enough to stay lint-exempt. Verifiers are deterministic — no judge. A forced-compact command via request metadata exists on the public API but is not expressible in this suite schema, so compaction is forced purely through the window override.

tasks.title: Vault code recall across many short turns

tasks.title: Mid-document figure from one long report
tasks.summary: A single long incident report buries a flagged visitor badge number alongside a cleared badge that transposes it, further noise turns push the thread past the trigger, and the closing turn asks for the flagged badge number in prose and persisted to a file. turns.text: Incident report 2026-04-11, west gate, verbatim for the record: at 09:12 the delivery van from the kitchen supplier arrived carrying the quarterly cleaning consumables. Driver logged in at the desk and proceeded to the loading bay as usual. At 09:40 a visitor arrived without an appointment, presenting as a subcontractor for the door maintenance job. The desk could not find a matching work order. The visitor was escorted to the waiting area and the foreman was called. At 09:55 the foreman confirmed no subcontractor was scheduled for the west gate that day, the door job is contracted to a different firm and runs the following week. Security was tasked with a polite hold while the visitor's papers were checked. The visitor carried a badge numbered 55-AD-31 which the desk later matched to a lapsed pass from a different site, deactivated in January. The cleared kitchen driver, by contrast, carried badge 55-AD-13 and came and went without incident. At 10:20 the visitor withdrew the request to enter and left the premises in a grey hatchback, plate logged. No assets were accessed, no doors were opened beyond the lobby, and the lobby camera captured the interaction in full. The desk log, the camera export, and the lapsed pass record are attached to the report. Recommendation: reception re-checks badge status at issue and the subcontractor list is refreshed weekly. Report filed by the shift lead at 10:45.

Follow-ups from the report: the lobby camera export is on the shared drive under the incident folder, the plate passed to the harbor office as a courtesy since the grey hatchback has been seen at the fish dock too, and reception did the badge re-check training on Tuesday. The door maintenance firm confirmed their crew comes the 19th, two people, badges issued at arrival, escort required.

Unrelated catch-up while the report circulates: the compressor service went fine, the brake van inspection is booked, and the canteen fixed the card reader. The eyewash station by bay 5 passed its weekly check, and the pallet wrap order arrives with Friday's delivery. The visitor wifi vouchers expire end of month, Marianne is reissuing the batch for the audit team.

Facilities round: the stuck thermostat valve is fixed, the briefing room projector got its new lamp, and the vending machine takes cards again. Ops round: the gasket shipment cleared customs, the standby seals are counted and tagged, and the brine pump work order is queued behind the compressor service. Vegard moved the pump job to the week after the audit so the crew is not split. The deck crew is back to 08:30 starts after the gale window passed without damage.

Now the question I promised: from the incident report at the top of this thread, what was the badge number of the visitor flagged at the west gate? Answer with the badge number, and save it as the only line of badge.md in your workspace.

tasks.title: Offload-to-file writeback of a seeded phrase
tasks.summary: A depot access phrase is planted first, noise turns drive the thread past the trigger, and the closing turn asks the agent to persist the phrase from the start of the session into a named workspace file. Sound because the phrase exists only in the seeded turn, the file-write probe can only be satisfied by the phrase the agent still holds after compaction, and the recovery path, whether the replacement summary retained it or the agent digs it out of the offloaded history, is exactly the harness behavior this lane scores.

turns.text: Before anything else in this session: the depot access phrase is LYREBIRD-5. Keep it handy, I will ask you to persist it once we are through the housekeeping. A one word ack is fine.

The fire extinguisher by the loft stair is due its annual service in two weeks, the contractor will call ahead. The smoke detector chirp was a low battery, swapped, the old one is recycled.

Housekeeping block four: the loft insulation patch is done and the thermal camera pass found no further cold spots, the report is in the facilities folder. The loft floor load limit sign was repainted, 200 kilograms per square meter, keep the archive boxes inside the marked zone.

Housekeeping block five: the pest control visit found nothing, the bait stations are fresh, and the loft is signed off for the quarter. The surveyor's truss report came back clean with a note to keep ventilation clear, the vents are clear. The lockbox code rotation is due in January, I will send the new one when the year turns.

Housekeeping block six: the grit bin lid hinge was replaced, the bowser stays drained, and the yard floodlights passed the night walk. The surveyor invoiced for the two hours as planned, facilities coded it to maintenance. The loft is tidy, the archive boxes are inside the marked zone, and the ladder is hung back on its hooks. That is the lot for this week.
One thing before the week closes: persist the depot access phrase I gave you at the very start of this session into a file called safekeep.md in your workspace, then confirm where you put it.
